why_angle: The cited OREI support pages rate one kit at 115 ft and another at 394 ft, and call both '4K60 4:4:4, 18 Gbps'. None says that HDBaseT before 3.0 carries 10.2 Gbps and needs compression for that signal, or that HDBaseT 3.0 is rated to only 328 ft uncompressed. This page puts every kit's 4K60 reach on the same basis and adds AV Access's 131 ft rating as an outside reference for an 18 Gbps HDBaseT link.

page.title: Best HDMI Extender Splitter over Cat6 for 4K60 (2026)
page.h1: Best HDMI extender splitter: which 4K60 distance ratings hold up
page.desc: HDMI extender splitters over Cat6 compared at 4K60: OREI's 115 ft kits, J-Tech's 196 ft kits and why a 394 ft HDBaseT 4K60 4:4:4 rating needs a closer look.
page.answer: Short answer. An HDMI extender splitter sends one source to several TVs over Cat6. Best: OREI UHD12-EX115-K (1x2) or UHD14-EX115-K (1x4), rated 115 ft at full 4K60 4:4:4, 18 Gbps. Uncompressed HDBaseT 3.0 tops out at 328 ft, so 394 ft 4K60 claims need checking.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Reach: J-Tech rates its kits at 196 ft at 4K@60Hz, 1.70 times OREI's 115 ft (196 ÷ 115). J-Tech gives 18 Gbps as the kit's maximum but doesn't give the colour format at that distance. OREI rates its 115 ft for 4:4:4.
  • Power per TV (rated maximum): UHD12-EX115-K 8.28 W ÷ 2 = 4.14 W; UHD14-EX115-K 14 W ÷ 4 = 3.5 W; JTECH-14EX60-AE 12.5 W ÷ 4 = 3.1 W; UHD14-EXB400-K 35 W ÷ 4 = 8.75 W, which is 2.8 times the J-Tech (8.75 ÷ 3.125).
  • Maker price per TV: JTECH-14EX60-AE $302.49 ÷ 4 = $75.62; JTECH-18EX60-AE $639.99 ÷ 8 = $80.00; UHD14-EXB400-K $429.00 ÷ 4 = $107.25. The 14EX60-AE and the EXB400-K were both listed as unavailable on their makers' stores on 2026-11-10.
Your setupFits
2 TVs within 115 ft, all 4KOREI UHD12-EX115-K
3–4 TVs within 115 ft, all 4KOREI UHD14-EX115-K
A 4K TV and an older 1080p TV on one sourceJ-Tech kits, which downscale 4K to 1080p at the receiver. The 1×4 is listed unavailable; the 1×8 JTECH-18EX60-AE is available.
Runs of 115–197 ftEither OREI 115 ft kit at 1080p60, which OREI rates to 197 ft
Runs past 197 ftAn HDBaseT kit, but read the next section first

Why 115 ft and 394 ft can't both be uncompressed 4K60 4:4:4

An 8-bit 4K60 4:4:4 HDMI signal is an 18 Gbps feed. HDBaseT links before version 3.0 carry 10.2 Gbps, so that signal has to be compressed to cross them. Installation magazine described exactly this in 2018: CYP's AVLC compression passes 4K60 4:4:4 over HDBaseT 'despite HDBaseT's 10.2Gbps bandwidth limitation'. The HDBaseT Alliance's own 2017 reference design carried full 18 Gbps HDMI 2.0 'using visually lossless compression'. HDBaseT 3.0 raised the link to 16 Gbps and, according to CE Pro (2019), carries fully uncompressed 4K60 4:4:4 'for up to 100m/328ft'.

OREI rates the UHD14-EXB400-K at 394 ft (120 m) for 4K60 4:4:4. That is 66 ft past the uncompressed HDBaseT 3.0 limit (394 − 328). OREI's store still calls the video 'uncompressed', and neither its store page nor its support article names an HDBaseT version or chipset. For comparison, AV Access rates its own 18 Gbps HDBaseT extender, the 4KEX70-H2, at 131 ft on Cat6a/7 and 115 ft on Cat5e/6 for 4K60 4:4:4. Those numbers match OREI's 115 ft kits, not its 394 ft one. The '230 ft' in AV Access's headline for that extender is its 1080p rating on Cat6a/7.

Not recommended

OREI UHD14-EXB400-K, if you need full 4K60 4:4:4 over very long runs. Its 394 ft 4K60 4:4:4 rating is longer than the uncompressed HDBaseT 3.0 limit. Its store page contradicts itself: the feature text gives 394 ft at 4K@60Hz, but the spec table lists 393 ft against 4K@30Hz. It was also listed as unavailable on OREI's store on 2026-11-10. Its 492 ft 1080p60 rating is the safer figure to plan around.
